title: Switched E212 MNC fields from type uint to string
description: Storing MNC as uint can cause loss of info when the mnc is prefixed with 0's. E.G. MNC=007 or MNC=01 (Prefixed 0's are lost). Storing MNC as a string fixes this.

notes.body: See #19114 for the ongoing discussion and why IMHO we should add an extra filter and not break a long standing filter.

The main problem I have is really the backward compatibility, thus my suggestion to add a PLMN filter with a string.
Still I'm open to discussion of curse and if the majority is OK with a filter type change, we can take this route.

Fix the bug > creating more nuance. End of the day, when we (telecommunications engineers), input mnc into a filter, it's because we're trying to target a specific mobile network carrier. To us, that's 007 or 01, not 7 or 1, because MNC is 2-3 digits. Initially the filter we think is right produces nothing. You actually have to know what Wireshark is doing to fashion a workaround to produce the correct filter (hence what we have now is an anti-pattern).

The backwards compatibility you're suggesting we keep is really workarounds for the real issue. If we have to filter 7 for 007, it's because we have to knowingly work around the bug.

Worse, when tshark -e outputs 7 instead of 007, when parsing traffic, how do we match that to a real MNC? Is it 07, 007? The data loss in tshark is drastic. Where, visually, Wireshark has it right in the details pane, tshark completely fails in this aspect.

I vote we actually fix MNC instead of leaving it broken. People will be happier over the next decade.
Let me discuss this with the dissector author during SharkFest next week to find a consensus.
We agreed to switch to strings in master branch (future wireshark 4.2), but both for MCC and MNC fields.

commits_data.title: E212: switch MCC and MNC fields from uint to string
commits_data.message:
E212: switch MCC and MNC fields from uint to string

Storing MCC and MNC as uint can cause loss of info when they are prefixed with 0's.
E.G. MNC=007 or MNC=01 (Prefixed 0's are lost). Storing them as a string fixes this.

Fixes #19114
